finding.frontend: Choosing an import reason reveals nothing. The captured screenshot of fe-import-reason-transit-selected shows Transit selected and the next thing on the page is the Save and continue button — no port of exit, no destination country. The follow-up questions are separate pages reached only after the user submits, in the fixed order purpose, destination country, port of exit, exit date (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:49-57), and the hub carries them as a second, conditional task row of their own (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:34-39). So Internal market costs a user two page loads, Transhipment or onward travel two, Transit three and Temporary admission horses three, where Design release 1 costs one. A user answering for transit therefore visits three pages and crosses two hub tasks to answer one question and its consequences. Two further differences travel with the split and disappear with it. First, each of the split-out pages says its own name three times — breadcrumb, page heading and field label — so fe-destination-country reads "Destination country / Destination country / Destination country" down the left of the page, from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/template.njk:8 and :16; fe-port-of-exit and fe-exit-date are the same shape. Second, each carries hint text that Design release 1's reveal does not: "The country the consignment travels on to after Great Britain." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/copy/copy.en.js:5) and the leading sentence of "The date the animals are expected to leave Great Britain. For example, 27/3/2026" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/copy/copy.en.js:5) — text a field only needs once it has been stranded on a page with no surrounding question. Both reasons that ask two questions ask them in the opposite order to Design release 1's: Transit asks destination country and then port of exit, and Temporary admission horses asks port of exit and then exit date, because the four pages sit in one fixed sequence and every reason walks the same sequence.
finding.prototype: The reason page answers itself. Each importReason radio that has follow-up questions opens them inline underneath it as a conditional reveal, so the user reads the reason, chooses it, answers what it needs and presses Save and continue once (app/views/reason-for-import.html:47-62). Internal market opens the "Purpose in the internal market" question with its eleven radios; Transhipment or onward travel opens a Destination country select; Transit opens Port of exit and then Destination country; Temporary admission horses opens Exit date and then Port of exit; Re-entry opens nothing. No reveal carries a page heading, and only two of them carry any text beyond a field label: the internal-market reveal heads its radios with a medium fieldset legend reading "Purpose in the internal market", and the exit date carries the worked example "For example, 27/3/2026". The other three fields are a bare label over a select, because the radio's own hint above them already supplies the context. Every reveal is present in the rendered page and hidden until its radio is chosen, which is why a captured temporary-admission state carries all six reveal fields in its DOM (app/routes.js:8778-8820). Six rather than four because Design release 1 gives each branch its own field name: it renders two destination-country selects and two port-of-exit selects on the one page, with identical labels, identical 41-entry and 10-entry lists and identical error text, and the review page collapses each pair back to a single row keyed on the reason. Two inputs cannot share a name attribute, so the per-branch prefixes are a DOM artefact rather than a sixth and seventh question, and nothing here asks Frontend to hold two of either field.
finding.difference: Move the four questions onto the reason page as conditional reveals under the radio that requires them, and delete the four pages, the conditional exit-details task row and the four page-name headings that go with them. Nothing has to land first: the two sides already agree exactly on when each question applies, so no obligation changes. src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js gates purposeInInternalMarket on internalMarket (:43-56), destinationCountry on transit or transhipmentOrOnwardTravel (:66-79), portOfExit on transit or temporaryAdmissionHorses (:86-99) and exitDate on temporaryAdmissionHorses (:103-116), and Design release 1 reveals exactly the same four sets. Take each reveal's internal order from Design release 1 — port of exit then destination country under Transit, and exit date then port of exit under Temporary admission horses. Once the questions sit under their radio, drop the destination-country hint and the leading sentence of the exit-date hint, keeping the worked example "For example, 27/3/2026" that Design release 1 also shows; that copy work is booked on its own as inc-068, and the Exit details hub row this change retires is booked as inc-069, so the three can be scheduled together or the reveal move taken on its own. What happens to an answer when the reason changes needs no decision of its own: both sides purge a reveal answer once its reason is no longer chosen — every Design release 1 POST to the reason page writes null to each branch field belonging to a reason other than the one submitted, and Frontend's obligation gates take the same four fields out of scope and purge them — so nothing about a flip moves either. If anything Frontend keeps more than Design release 1 does, because its single destinationCountry field serves both Transit and Transhipment, so a country answered under Transit is still in scope under Transhipment where Design release 1's transhipment field starts empty; that is the same per-branch-naming artefact and not a requirement.
finding.correction: Two things were claimed more broadly than the evidence supports and both slots have been fixed. (1) The prototype slot said "The four reveals carry no page heading and no field hint of their own." The exit-date reveal does carry a hint — dr1-reason-for-import-temporary-admission-revealed.html:1067-1077 renders the label "Exit date" over the hint "For example, 27/3/2026", and the screenshot shows it — and the internal-market reveal carries a medium fieldset legend, "Purpose in the internal market" (:306-310). The rest of the claim holds: no reveal has a page heading and the three select fields carry a label only. This matters to the work, because the difference in the exit-date hint is the leading sentence alone, which the frontend slot already said correctly. (2) The order claim named Transit only. Temporary admission horses is reversed too: Design release 1 asks exit date and then port of exit (labels at :1067 and :1146), while the frontend's fixed page sequence gives port of exit before exit date (flow.js:54-55). Both slots now say so. Nothing else in the finding changed. "importReason" was added to controls so the crop resolves on the Design release 1 side as well, where the radio group is named importReason rather than reasonForImport.
finding.falsifiedBy: A conditional reveal opening under any importReason radio on the frontend. The captured DOM of fe-import-reason has no govuk-radios__conditional element at all and no aria-controls on any of the five radios; finding one would prove this wrong.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs (capture/html/frontend/fe-import-reason.html, fe-import-reason-transit-selected.html, fe-import-purpose.html, fe-destination-country.html, fe-port-of-exit.html, fe-exit-date.html and capture/html/prototype/dr1-reason-for-import.html plus its four revealed states) and opened the fe-import-reason-transit-selected, dr1-reason-for-import-transit-revealed and dr1-reason-for-import-temporary-admission-revealed screenshots. Ran the falsifier: grep for govuk-radios__conditional returns 0 hits on fe-import-reason and 4 on dr1-reason-for-import, and no frontend radio carries aria-controls. Re-read flow.js:49-57, task-rows.js:34-39 and every cited obligation line range; all resolve to what the sentence says. Rubric 2 (overstatement) and rubric 5 (missing finding) fired — see correction. The purge-on-flip claim folded in from the parallel run was checked the same way, by reading every reference to the five branch fields in app/routes.js against the frontend obligation gates: Design release 1 nulls the other branches' fields on every reason submit, in both the proceed and the soft-save paths, so neither side keeps a stale answer and there is no data decision hiding inside this change.

openQuestions: Does any conditional-reveal answer on the import reason page need to be provable without JavaScript, and if so who owns that test? Deleting src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/exit-date.fit.spec.js removed its `test.use({ javaScriptEnabled: false })` block — the only no-JS coverage of a moj-datepicker field, which asserted a typed 27/3/2026 exit date persists and that no 'Choose date' button renders — and nothing on the reason page replaced it. A repo-wide grep for javaScriptEnabled now returns only origin.fit.spec.js:315 and arrival-transit.fit.spec.js:251,371, and none of those three opens a conditional reveal (origin's deliberately takes the 'No' branch). So all four reveal answers — purpose, destination country, port of exit and exit date — are now unproven without JavaScript, and because the questions no longer have pages of their own there is no other route to them: if govuk-frontend's gating of .govuk-radios__conditional--hidden behind .govuk-frontend-supported ever regresses, every follow-up question becomes permanently unreachable for no-JS users with nothing in the suite failing. DEFERRED rather than fixed in this increment because it is not a like-for-like port: the deleted block tested an always-visible field on a page of its own, whereas the equivalent here has to assert a govuk-frontend gating behaviour (reveals rendered visible when the enhancement script never runs) that this repo has never asserted anywhere, so it is a new class of coverage and a new browser context on the increment's critical path rather than a restored assertion. ACTION: decide whether progressive enhancement of conditional reveals is in this service's test contract. If yes, add a `test.use({ javaScriptEnabled: false })` describe to src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-reason/import-reason.fit.spec.js that checks the temporaryAdmissionHorses radio, types 27/3/2026 into #temporaryAdmissionExitDate, selects #temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit, submits, and asserts both answers come back on reload plus that the 'Choose date' button has count 0 — and consider the same shape for the other three reveals. If no, record here that no-JS reveal behaviour is govuk-frontend's contract and is deliberately untested in this repo.

Should Lighthouse audit the import reason page in each of its reveal states, now that the four pages it used to audit those controls on are gone? Before this increment, scripts/lighthouse/audit-targets.js routed /destination-country, /port-of-exit and /exit-date to seeded notifications through FILLED_BY, so each control was audited visible on a page of its own. After it, FILLED_BY names only '/notifications/{journeyId}/confirmation' -> submitted and '/notifications/{journeyId}/transporters/private' -> transit (audit-targets.js:40-43), and /import-reason is audited only on the draft shape, whose reason is internalMarket (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/fixtures/happy-path.json). govukRadios renders every unchosen branch's conditional inside .govuk-radios__conditional--hidden (display:none), which axe and Lighthouse skip, so transitPortOfExit, transitDestinationCountry, transhipmentDestinationCountry, temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit and the mojDatePicker at import-reason/template.njk:66 — five controls this increment introduces — are never audited in a visible state anywhere. DEFERRED rather than fixed in this increment because the orphaned `temporaryAdmission` seed shape is being deleted here (dead work: seed-audit-targets.js walked a whole notification no audited URL used), and the alternative — auditing the same route under more than one notification shape — is a structural change to FILLED_BY, auditUrls and reportNames, which today assume one shape per path and one report name per route, plus a way to open a reveal before the audit runs. That is a Lighthouse-harness redesign, not a fix to this diff. ACTION: decide with the team whether reveal-state accessibility is audited by Lighthouse or left to the fit-spec axe runs in import-reason.fit.spec.js (which do scan with a reveal open). If Lighthouse is to cover it, allow a route to be audited under several shapes — e.g. /import-reason on both draft and a reason-per-branch shape — and reinstate a seed shape per audited reason with a report name that distinguishes them.
